title: Time-Varying Mutual Information Decoding for Mitigating Visual Forgetting in Vision-Language Models

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to counteract progressive visual forgetting during long chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language models (VLMs). Paper [8] explicitly addresses "visual forgetting in video reasoning" caused by "visual anchor drifting," which is conceptually equivalent to the contribution's purpose. Both aim to mitigate the degradation of visual grounding during extended reasoning processes, even though [8] focuses on video reasoning rather than general VLM inference.

### Mechanism
The contribution introduces a time-varying mutual information decoding mechanism that amplifies the difference between image-conditioned and image-masked logits, with a correction weight increasing over generation steps via an exponential schedule. Paper [27] discusses time-varying decoding in convolutional codes, which is conceptually similar in its use of dynamic programming to adjust decoding weights over time. Additionally, paper [10] analyzes mutual information loss in decoding, and paper [16] discusses maximum mutual information decoding in space-time block codes. While these papers do not address VLMs or hallucination mitigation, the underlying primitive of time-varying mutual information decoding is covered across these works.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates its method using HallusionBench and MMStar benchmarks, reporting accuracy improvements. Paper [30] introduces HallusionBench as a benchmark for evaluating hallucination in VLMs, making the evaluation design covered. Additionally, papers [1], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [14], and [31] all use similar evaluation designs for hallucination mitigation in VLMs, employing standard benchmarks and metrics to validate their methods. The use of HallusionBench and MMStar is a change of benchmark instance, not a new evaluation design.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of vision-language model inference and hallucination mitigation during decoding. Papers [1], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [11], [14], [17], [29], and [31] all address hallucination mitigation in VLMs, which is the same general application area. While some focus on specific sub-problems (e.g., medical VLMs in [4] and [7]), the domain is clearly covered.

**PURPOSE: Counteract progressive visual forgetting during long chain-of-thought reasoning in VLMs.**

Paper [8] "When Thinking Hurts: Mitigating Visual Forgetting in Video Reasoning via Frame Repetition" directly addresses "visual anchor drifting" where models increasingly rely on self-generated text during extended CoT reasoning, sidelining visual inputs — this is substantively the same objective of counteracting progressive visual forgetting during long chain-of-thought reasoning in VLMs. Paper [1] (CRoPS) also notes "effectiveness declines toward the end of generation, where hallucinations are most likely to occur," which partially overlaps, but [8] is the clearest match.

---

**MECHANISM: Time-varying mutual information decoding with exponential schedule gamma_t amplifying (l_c - l_u) difference, gated by confidence threshold.**

The core primitive has two parts: (a) contrastive decoding amplifying image-conditioned vs. image-masked logit differences, and (b) a time-varying/dynamic weight that increases over generation steps, gated by confidence.

For (a): Papers [6], [17], [5], [14], [31], [4], [7] all use contrastive decoding that amplifies the difference between image-conditioned and image-degraded/masked logits — this is the same primitive of l_c - l_u amplification.

For (b) the time-varying exponential schedule: Paper [1] (CRoPS) explicitly addresses declining effectiveness toward end of generation and builds a hallucination model that compensates — it uses a position-aware correction. Paper [14] (Octopus) uses dynamic contrastive decoding that adapts weights per token. Paper [19] (Uncertainty-Aware Contrastive Decoding) uses dynamic weighting between models based on uncertainty. Paper [12] (Thinking by Subtraction) uses confidence-driven contrastive decoding for LLM reasoning with a confidence gate.

The specific combination of: exponential time-varying gamma_t increasing over steps + confidence-based gate (max prob < alpha) applied to VLM contrastive decoding is most closely approximated by combining [1] (time-varying correction over generation) + [14] (dynamic per-token weighting) + [19] (uncertainty/confidence-based dynamic weighting). Paper [12] uses confidence-driven contrastive decoding with a gate. Paper [1] explicitly uses a correction weight that varies over generation position. The underlying primitives — dynamic/adaptive contrastive decoding weight + confidence gating — are covered by [1], [14], [19], and [12] collectively. The exponential schedule is a specific parameterization of "increasing weight over time," which is the same primitive as [1]'s position-aware correction. I'll cite [1] as the primary cover for the combined mechanism.

---

**EVALUATION: HallusionBench aAcc and MMStar metrics on VLAA-Thinker-7B.**

HallusionBench is a named benchmark used in prior VLM hallucination work. Paper [30] introduces hallucination evaluation frameworks for LVLMs. Papers [1], [3], [6], [14] all evaluate on standard VLM hallucination benchmarks (POPE, MME, HallusionBench family). The evaluation design — measuring aAcc on HallusionBench and accuracy on MMStar — uses existing named benchmarks with standard metrics. This is a standard evaluation design (named benchmark + accuracy metric) used across many prior papers in this space, e.g., [1], [6], [14]. The design is covered.

---

**DOMAIN: Vision-language model inference / hallucination mitigation (training-free decoding).**

Numerous prior papers ([1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [11], [14], [17], [31]) operate in exactly this domain: training-free decoding for hallucination mitigation in VLMs.
